title: SQS redelivery and idempotency
objectives: Explain that an SQS event source mapping polls and batches records.
Trace how a batch failure can replay records whose side effects already committed.
Explain the partial batch response boundary and its ordering assumptions.
Design an atomic idempotency key and a bounded poison-record path.
assumptions: Standard SQS queue with a Lambda event source mapping; records can be delivered more than once.
A, B, and C are independent records for the partial-batch illustration; ordered-stream semantics are out of scope.
Database commit for A and B occurs before the invocation reports failure for C.
Visibility duration is conceptual. Configure it using current AWS guidance for the function timeout and batching window.
Partial batch response reduces unnecessary replay; it does not make delivery exactly once.
hinglish: Event source mapping SQS ko poll karke batch banati hai. Agar A aur B ka DB write commit ho gaya, lekin C fail hua, whole batch failure par A aur B phir deliver ho sakte hain. Partial batch response mein sirf failed message IDs return karo. Phir bhi visibility timeout ke baad C dobara aa sakta hai. Isliye business key par atomic idempotency, bounded retry, DLQ, aur queue-age monitoring saath design karo.

sources.supports: poll-based event source mapping and queue/stream delivery
batch failure and partial batch response behavior
SQS mapping and visibility timeout configuration
message invisibility and redelivery after visibility expiry

checkpoints.prompt: A and B committed, but the batch reports failure for C. What protects A and B if they are delivered again?
options: An atomic idempotency key in durable storage
checkpoints.feedback: Sahi. Visibility controls when retry can happen; atomic durable idempotency controls duplicate business effects.

checkpoints.prompt: With independent SQS records and partial batch response enabled, what should the handler return?
options: An empty response even if C failed
checkpoints.feedback: Return failed item identifiers only. Confirm independence and ordering semantics before using this pattern.
